title: Visual constraints upon avian behaviour
why: A Cardiff PhD thesis on how avian behaviour is constrained by eye design: eye size, retinal image brightness and retinal topographic analysis compared across bird species (stored abstract). The harvest listed it for four of the six Colluricincla queries ("Colluricincla vision", "Colluricincla spectral sensitivity opsin", "Colluricincla visual acuity" and "Colluricincla visual field"), and OpenAlex search appears to match words in the full text (my inference from its returning a thesis whose abstract names no species), so a grey shrikethrush may be named in its comparisons. Retinal topography gives peak cell density and from it acuity (acuity_cpd) and receptor spacing (interreceptor_deg). The screen tool lists it as the one candidate for those two traits (words: eye size, retina). Green open copy; not opened by this desk. The same thesis is already on the wanted list for Oriolus (harvest-37).

title: Evolution of color and vision of butterflies
why: Elymnias: a hit of the family review "Nymphalidae vision review" in this genus's harvest (the listing stores no abstract, so no keyword flagged it). The title says it covers the colour and vision of butterflies, and main's evidence file oa-12.jsonl logs from its abstract alone (authors Stavenga DG and Arikawa K) that nymphalid butterflies share a basic set of ultraviolet-, blue- and green-sensitive receptors, so the full text may tabulate the photoreceptor spectra of nymphalid species that include an Elymnias species (lambda_max_nm, spectral_range_nm). The same review is on the wanted lists of harvest-30 (for skippers) and harvest-35 (for Aporia and Hamadryas). The harvest listing does not show the authors or the journal; both are copied from main's wanted line for this paper in harvest-35.jsonl. Not opened. title: Opponent processing in the retinal mosaic of nymphalid butterflies
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
why: Apatura: listed by the screen tool for acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg (words: facet, ommatidi, retina) and returned by the genus queries "Apatura vision" and "Apatura eye". Its stored abstract starts: "The eyes of nymphalid butterflies, investigated with incident illumination, show colourful facet reflection patterns, the eye shine ... Here, we analyse the retinae of two nymphalids, Apatura ilia, which has a uniform eyeshine, and Charaxes jasius ... using single-cell recordings, spectroscopy and optical pupillometry. Apatura has UV-, blue- and green-sensitive photoreceptors, allocated into three ..." (cut off at 700 characters). The abstract start does not reach a facet size or an ommatidial angle, and a paper that analyzes the ommatidia and eye-shine facet map of Apatura ilia may give facet diameters, an ommatidial angle or a pseudopupil measurement (acuity_cpd, interommatidial_deg). Main already logs Apatura ilia receptor classes from another paper (insects-met.jsonl, 10.1098/rspb.2021.1560). Authors are not shown in the harvest listing. Not opened. The bioRxiv preprint of the same work (10.1101/2022.02.10.479932, green open copy) was listed beside it. The desk's web pair for the acuity traits ("Apatura visual acuity" and "purple emperor visual acuity") returned human and clinical acuity pages, patents, a bird acuity compilation, the Empoasca onukii acuity paper (a leafhopper), colour-code pages for "Purple Emperor" and a DTIC report shown without a readable title; none names an Apatura acuity or ommatidial angle, and none was opened.
get: open access (hybrid per OpenAlex): https://doi.org/10.1098/rstb.2021.0275; green preprint copy: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2022/02/10/2022.02.10.479932.full.pdf

title: The eye of the domesticated sheep with implications for vision
why: Ovis fov_h_deg: this paper came back in both desk web searches for the visual field ("Ovis visual field" and "sheep visual field"), as a Cambridge Core page whose address reads eye-of-the-domesticated-sheep-with-implications-for-vision in the journal Animal Science. Main's evidence file mammals-met.jsonl logs from its abstract alone that visual fields were measured in 10 sheep and that a binocular field is present, with "degrees not in abstract" and "number wanted from the full text", so the full text should give the horizontal field of view of Ovis aries. Field of view travels within a genus (carry rule 3), so a number for the domestic sheep would also fix the other Ovis species listed. The two visual-field searches also returned human and bird visual-field pages and patents, farm-blog pages on sheep pupils and eyes, the Wikipedia article on the visual field and five records shown without readable titles (PubMed Central PMC1309321, a huveta.hu record, a SERVAL notice and two digitum.um.es addresses); none of those was opened and any could bear on the same row. The line merges with main's existing wanted line for the goat and cattle views (web-mammals.jsonl), from which the authors, year, journal and DOI are copied. Not opened.

title: Sheep (Ovis aries)
why: Ovis fov_h_deg and absolute_sensitivity: a hit of the harvest query "Ovis vision" (closed access). Its stored abstract lists a section on "behaviour in light and darkness (vision)" beside sections on senses, on behaviour in danger or peril and on active and resting patterns, so the chapter may state the field of view of sheep (fov_h_deg) and how sheep see and behave in dim light (absolute_sensitivity). A behaviour chapter is a secondary source and may repeat primary papers such as the sheep eye paper on the line above. The harvest listing does not show the authors. why: Regiscolia colour_vision and spectral_range_nm: a hit of the harvest's family review query "Scoliidae vision review" (a green open-access copy on Zenodo). The title names visual and olfactory cues for catching scoliid wasps, so the paper may report which trap colours the wasps came to, and the brief takes behavioural evidence for colour_vision. The stored abstract is only a citation line (Vuts, Razov, Kaydan and Tóth 2012, Acta Zoologica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 58(4): 351-359, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5735977, a second Zenodo DOI beside the harvest's 10.5281/zenodo.5735976), so the species caught are not visible and the paper may name no Regiscolia (Megascolia) species. A gcris.yyu.edu.tr record of the same title also came up in the desk's web search "Mammoth Scoliid Wasp visual acuity". The desk's spectral web searches ("Regiscolia spectral sensitivity" and "Mammoth Scoliid Wasp spectral sensitivity") are described in the lambda_max_nm and receptor_classes records of this unit; none of their result titles names a scoliid pigment, spectral range or colour test. Not opened.
